title: 1.4.17 Where Does the Balance Live?
description: A bank account, two paradigms. Say where the depositing code goes in each, and when you'd want which. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Where Does the Balance Live? — AI-graded rubric
aiGrader.prompt:
A program keeps track of a bank account: it stores a balance, and it needs code that deposits money into that balance.

1. In object-oriented style, where does the code that changes the balance live? Say where, and say why that placement is what makes the style object-oriented.

2. In procedural style, where would that same code live instead?

3. Name one situation where procedural is the better fit, and one where object-oriented is. Give a reason for each - not just a preference.

rubric.title: Q1: the behaviour lives with the data
rubric.description: Student says the depositing code lives in the account object itself, alongside the balance. Deny if the answer places it in a separate procedure, or is too vague to tell where it went.

rubric.title: Q1: names bundling as what makes it object-oriented
rubric.description: Student connects the placement to the paradigm - that bundling data with the behaviour acting on it is exactly what makes the style object-oriented. Credit any clear statement of that link. Deny if Q1 only states the placement with no reason attached.

rubric.title: Q2: procedural keeps them separate
rubric.description: Student says that in procedural style the depositing code sits in a separate procedure/function, away from the balance, which is held in its own variable. Deny if the contrast is missing or if the answer describes the same arrangement twice.

rubric.title: Q3: one situation each, with reasons
rubric.description: Student names a situation suiting procedural (typically a small, direct job or a short script) and one suiting object-oriented (typically a larger program, or many similar things each keeping their own data), and gives a reason for each. Deny if either situation is missing, or if reasons are bare preference such as 'it's cleaner'.
